identity.name: Plain caramel
identity.chemical_class: Class I caramel colour; process-derived complex carbohydrate caramelization products

function.mechanism: Controlled thermal treatment of carbohydrates forms brown chromophoric polymers that impart color to foods and beverages.

adi.basis: EFSA group ADI for caramel colours E150a, E150b, E150c, and E150d (sum of four classes).

efsa.key_finding: EFSA set a group ADI of 300 mg/kg bw/day in 2011 and refined exposure in 2012 showed most population estimates below ADI, with upper-bound high toddler scenarios nearest to/slightly above ADI.

adi.basis: JECFA INS 150a entry lists ADI as not specified.

concerns.summary: Carcinogenic concern in caramel-color discussions is mainly tied to 4-methylimidazole (4-MEI), which IARC classifies as Group 2B; this concern is more associated with ammonia caramel classes than plain caramel.
Recent rodent studies report reproductive endpoints for 4-MEI at experimental exposures, but these are not direct E150a-only dietary studies.

no_concern_confirmed: JECFA INS 150a entry reports ADI as not specified.
FDA Title 21 lists caramel as GRAS under GMP and as a permitted food color under GMP.
EFSA refined exposure (2012) generally remained below the group ADI for most population groups.

adi_exceedance.notes: EFSA exceedance concern was modeled for grouped caramel colours (E150a-d), not specifically isolated to E150a.

risk_assessment.rationale: Regulators continue to permit E150a with GMP/ADI controls, JECFA lists ADI not specified for INS 150a, and the main serious signals are driven by related contaminants (notably 4-MEI) rather than strong direct evidence against plain caramel itself.
key_factors: EFSA group ADI 300 mg/kg bw/day for E150a-d
EFSA 2012 refined exposure mostly below ADI
FDA GRAS listing (21 CFR 182.1235) and food color listing (21 CFR 73.85)
No direct IARC classification found for E150a itself
